lessons.title: 1. Standard For Loops
lessons.description: C++ `for` loops iterate over ranges. Implement `sum_range(int start, int end)`.

exercises.question: Implement `factorial(int n)` returning n! as a long long, with 0! defined as 1. Accumulate in a loop the way `sum_range` does.

lessons.title: 2. While Loops
lessons.description: C++ `while` loops repeat while a condition holds true. Implement `count_digits(int n)`.

lessons.title: 3. Fibonacci Sequence (Concept Challenge)
lessons.description: Calculate the Nth Fibonacci number iteratively in C++.

lessons.title: 4. Power Calculator (Practice)
lessons.description: Practice: implement power(int base, int exp) returning base^exp as a long long, multiplying base into an accumulator exp times. The test asserts power(2, 5) == 32.
learning_objectives: Accumulate product in C++ for loop

options: the loop should start at `int i = 1` so the exponent is counted
`result` should be initialised to 0 so the first multiply seeds it
`i <= exp` runs one multiplication too many; it should be `i < exp`
exercises.correct_answer: `i <= exp` runs one multiplication too many; it should be `i < exp`
exercises.explanation: Starting `result` at 1 and multiplying `exp` times is the whole algorithm; looping to `<= exp` performs exp + 1 multiplications. Initialising `result` to 0 would make every answer 0.

lessons.title: 5. Unit 3 Checkpoint: C++ Loops Mastery
lessons.description: Checkpoint for loops: implement count_multiples(int start, int end, int k) counting every integer i in [start, end] where i % k == 0. The test asserts count_multiples(1, 15, 3) == 5.

exercises.question: Implement `count_vowels(std::string s)` returning how many characters are a, e, i, o or u (lower case only). Count inside a loop, as `count_multiples` does.
